symptomShortText: Cracks at retainer flange radius after forming

causesIshikawa.description: EMP-8140, Shift A - press setup verified against the setup sheet
EQ-PRESS09-001 tonnage and shut height logged within tolerance
DOC-10450 Rev A - forming sequence and radii unchanged since qualification
Coil lot COIL-6612 delivered as DC04 but hardness 214 HV and elongation 11% match DC01 full-hard; supplier shipped the wrong grade against the same part number
Hardness tester GA-0620, last cal 2026-06-09, R&R 3.9%

fiveWhyChain.question: Why do the retainers crack at the flange radius?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Elongation measured 11% against a 22% minimum, so the material cannot survive the forming strain

fiveWhyChain.question: Why is elongation half of specification?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Coil lot COIL-6612 has hardness 214 HV against a 160 HV maximum, consistent with a full-hard grade rather than the specified DC04

fiveWhyChain.question: Why did a wrong-grade coil enter production? (root cause)
fiveWhyChain.answer: Incoming inspection for this part number checks dimensions and surface only; there is no mechanical property check to catch a grade substitution

actions.actionText: Quarantine all SR8 from COIL-6612 and hardness-test every remaining coil in the store
Return coil lot COIL-6612 to the supplier and raise a supplier corrective action request
Add hardness and elongation checks to the incoming inspection plan for all formed-steel part numbers

lessonsLearned.whatWorked: Coil-level traceability tied all 1,240 cracked parts to a single delivery within a day
lessonsLearned.whatDidnt: Incoming inspection could not distinguish two grades that look identical and share a part number

isIsNot.isWhereWhenItHappens: SR8 retainers formed from coil lot COIL-6612
isIsNot.isNotWhereWhenItDoesnt: SR8 from coil lots COIL-6588 and COIL-6640 - same press, same die, same operators
isIsNot.notes: Defect tracks the coil lot exclusively

customerReference.complaintReference: N/A - internal defect, no customer reference
